name: Centrus Energy
description: Centrus sells enriched uranium fuel to nuclear utilities and is trying to rebuild US uranium enrichment. About three quarters of revenue comes from its LEU segment, which mostly resells enrichment work (measured in separative work units, SWU) bought from suppliers, including Russia's TENEX under a contract that runs through 2028, and adds natural uranium for utilities; it does not yet enrich commercial volumes itself. The smaller Technical Solutions segment is paid by the US Department of Energy to run a demonstration line in Piketon, Ohio, that makes HALEU (high-assay low-enriched uranium), the fuel for many new reactors such as Oklo's, at about 900 kilograms a year. The company's argument is scarcity: US law banned Russian LEU imports from August 2024 (waivers possible), Russia restricted exports to the US, and US buyers want a domestic supplier. It announced a large expansion of enrichment capacity at Piketon on September 25, 2025 and began commercial centrifuge production at Oak Ridge in December 2025, with the first new machines in Ohio expected in 2029. 2025 revenue was 448.7 million dollars and net income 77.8 million; it raised 805 million of zero-coupon convertible notes (2032) in August 2025 and holds 1.87 billion dollars of cash at June 30, 2026 to fund the build-out.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source. SEC SIC code 1400 (Mining and Quarrying of Nonmetallic Minerals). Centrus is a nuclear fuel trader and enrichment developer, not a miner.

hq.note: City and state from the EDGAR submissions record; operations in Piketon, Ohio and Oak Ridge, Tennessee

businessLines.name: LEU segment
businessLines.how: Long-term supply contracts with utilities priced per SWU (backlog of about 2.9 billion dollars reaching to 2040), buying SWU from suppliers and reselling at a margin; uranium sales are opportunistic and lumpy (uranium revenue fell 54% in 2025 while SWU revenue rose 21%).
businessLines.description: Sells the enrichment component (SWU) and, sometimes, natural uranium of low-enriched uranium fuel to utilities that run commercial reactors, sourced from a global network of suppliers, including TENEX.

revenue.note: SWU 298.7 million (+21%, volume +23%, price -1%) plus uranium 47.5 million (-54%); 2024: 349.9. H1 2026: SWU 141.6 plus uranium 56.4 million.

operatingProfit.note: Segment gross profit (segment operating income is not reported separately in the excerpt read); 2024: 93.9

businessLines.name: Technical Solutions segment
businessLines.how: Government contracts (cost-share and task-order based): DOE pays for operating the HALEU cascade and other engineering work; backlog about 0.9 billion dollars to 2034. A one-time development contract with the government is turning into a production contract only as DOE issues task orders.
businessLines.description: Advanced uranium enrichment and engineering, manufacturing and operations services, mainly for the DOE's HALEU Operation Contract (a cascade of 16 centrifuges at Piketon producing HALEU), plus HALEU production and deconversion contracts awarded October 2024 (IDIQ, task-order based).

brands.name: Piketon, Ohio (HALEU cascade and planned LEU/HALEU expansion)
brands.segment: Technical Solutions and future LEU production
brands.share: Demonstration cascade of 16 AC100M centrifuges; enrichment operations began October 11, 2023; annual rate 900 kg HALEU UF6 under Phase 2 of the HALEU Operation Contract

brands.name: Oak Ridge, Tennessee (centrifuge manufacturing)
brands.share: Commercial centrifuge production began December 2025; first new centrifuges expected online in Ohio in 2029; announced in January 2026 an investment plan of more than 560 million dollars (period and detail truncated in the extract)

brands.name: TENEX supply contract
brands.share: Contract through 2028; Russian Federal Decree No. 1544 (November 14, 2024) withdrew TENEX's general licence to export LEU to the US, extended through December 31, 2027 by later action; US import ban effective August 11, 2024 subject to DOE waivers
